notes.1ai: Candidates were able to provide very accurate frequency tables with only a few slips. The tally column was sometimes used instead of the frequency column for the answer.
notes.1aii: Many candidates gave the correct answer for the modal value.
notes.1aiii: Candidates should be encouraged to understand the difference between mean and median.
notes.1aiv: Candidates generally gave the correct answer. The common error was to not use the 24–hour clock as stated in the question but to write down 11 50 pm. A few candidates misread the hours and minutes hands.
notes.1bi: Many candidates gave the correct answer.
notes.1bii: Many candidates gave the correct answer but some gave an incomplete answer stating 10 – 16.
notes.1biii: Candidates found this part challenging. Many simply described the shape of the bar chart. Very few gave a comparison involving either the mode or mean or range or total number of trains.
notes.2a: The majority of candidates gave the correct answers although their spelling could be improved. Some candidates mixed up isosceles and equilateral.
notes.2bi: Many candidates gave the correct answer. The most common error was to just add up the four lengths given and not include the lengths which needed to be found.
notes.2bii: Those candidates who gave the correct answer for part (b)(i) tended to give the correct answer here as well. Most candidates used a sensible method of dividing up the area but arithmetic errors were sometimes seen when working was shown. Some candidates did not fully read the question and omitted the units.
notes.2ci: Very few candidates gave the correct answer. The common error was to write it is a right-angled triangle or to write about tangents, chords and diameters.
notes.2cii: Many candidates recognised that they needed to use Pythagoras’ theorem but some used it incorrectly by assuming AC was the hypotenuse. Some candidates assumed the triangle was isosceles.
notes.2ciii: Some candidates gave the full correct answer showing all their working. Some candidates did not show any working and gave an answer which was not accurate so lost all the marks. The other common error was to not halve the area of the circle.
notes.3ai: Nearly all candidates gave the correct answers.
notes.3aii: Although the vast majority of candidates drew the correct line quite a few did not draw it accurately.
notes.3b: Many candidates gave the correct answer. However, some did not fully read the question and gave an answer which was not in its simplest form.
notes.3c: Some candidates found this part challenging. Many understood that they needed to use 64 but o o linked it with 90 rather than 360 .
notes.4a: Many candidates completed the construction carefully and accurately. The common error was to not show arcs.
notes.4b: Fewer candidates completed this part correctly. There were a considerable number of candidates who drew a line bisector rather than an angle bisector.
notes.4c: When a point D had been identified nearly all candidates could measure the length of BD accurately.
notes.4d: Many candidates gave the wrong angle. The most common incorrect answers were to look at the bearing of A from C or to measure the bearing in the anti-clockwise direction.
notes.5a: Many candidates gave the correct answer but even more only gave the interest rather than the total amount as asked for in the question. Few candidates attempted to use compound interest.
notes.5b: Although nearly all candidates understood they needed to multiply 28 by 15.85 a considerable number didn’t recognise that this was money and an exact answer and gave answers to 3 significant figures.
notes.5c: The vast majority of candidates understood how to work out the total to pay and gave the correct answer. In general the main errors were caused by inaccurate multiplication or addition.
notes.5d: Nearly all candidates gave the correct answer with little or no working evident in the working space.
notes.5e: Some candidates gave the correct answer. Working was often poorly presented and hard to follow. A few candidates assumed there were 100 minutes in an hour.
notes.5f: Some candidates gave the correct answer. The most common error was to perform the multiplication in full and then round that answer to 1 significant figure. The other common error was to estimate 7.95 as 8 but leave 21 unrounded.
notes.6a: The vast majority of candidates gave the correct answer. The two most common errors were to misread the starting point as being at the origin (09 00) or to misread the horizontal scale as 09 10.
notes.6b: Most candidates understood where B was on the travel graph and gave the correct answer.
notes.6c: Most candidates gave the correct answer.
notes.6d: This part proved challenging for many candidates. Many split the travel into two sections when the train was in motion and averaged those two answers and ignored the time when the train was stopped. Some candidates incorrectly changed the time travelled into minutes or used 2.30.
notes.6ei: A small majority of candidates drew the correct travel graph. Many other candidates started the second train from A instead of C .
notes.6eii: Many candidates could read off the time when the trains crossed. However, there was evidence that some candidates misread the scale.
notes.6f: Most candidates correctly multiplied the two numbers together. However, many did not give the exact answer.
notes.7a: A few candidates gave the correct answer. Many forgot the minus sign or misread the scale for the intercept.
notes.7bi: The majority of candidates completed the table correctly. The common error was calculating the value when x = – 3 with the negative sign being mishandled.
notes.7bii: Many candidates plotted the points correctly although a large number misread the vertical scale. Drawing the curve was good although many candidates did not join the points to create a curve or drew straight lines between their plotted points.
notes.7biii: Candidates understood how to find the intersection but many of them misread the scale or forgot the minus sign for one of the answers.
notes.8ai: Candidates clearly demonstrated how to insert a value into a formula although some showed no working and lost marks when they gave an incorrect answer. The common incorrect answer was to not give an answer to 1 decimal place as asked for in the question.
notes.8aii: Candidates could generally simplify the a terms but had problems when simplifying the b terms due to the negative signs.
notes.8aiii: Nearly all candidates gave the correct answer. The common error was to divide instead of multiply giving an incorrect answer of 2.
notes.8aiv: Nearly all candidates gave the correct answer. The common error was to subtract instead of add giving an incorrect answer of 7.
notes.8b: Candidates found this part challenging. Although some gave the correct answer, a few of these did not show any working as stated in the question. Some candidates who did show working did not lay it out neatly and logically. Many candidates made errors in adding and subtracting.
notes.9ai: Nearly all candidates gave the correct answer.
notes.9aii: Many candidates gave the correct answer. Some candidates gave the rule for finding the general term rather than the next term.
notes.9aiii: Some candidates gave the correct answer. The common error was to write n+3 as the answer.
notes.9aiv: Very few candidates gave the correct answer. The common error was to say that 300 is a large number so would not be in the sequence.
notes.9bi: Nearly all candidates gave the correct answer.
notes.9bii: Very few candidates gave the correct answer. Good attempts were seen which did not quite give the correct answer. For example, stating adding one to previous number rather than adding one to the previous difference.
notes.10a: Nearly all candidates plotted the points accurately.
notes.10b: Many candidates made a good attempt at drawing the line of best fit. The most common errors were to just join up the points with straight lines or to join up the corners of the graph.
notes.10c: The majority of candidates gave the correct answer. Most of the remaining candidates gave an answer of positive even though they had drawn a line with a negative gradient.
notes.10d: Many candidates showed a good ability to read values from their line of best fit.
notes.10e: Many candidates showed a good ability to read values from their line of best fit.
notes.11a: Some candidates gave the correct answer. The common error was to reflect the triangle in a different line from the given one.
notes.11b: Many candidates gave the correct answer. The common error was to assume the translation vector was the co-ordinates of one of the points of the new shape.
notes.11ci: Many candidates only partially described the single transformation. Others described it as two transformations – usually a rotation plus a translation.
notes.11cii: Many candidates only partially described the single transformation. Others described it as two transformations – usually an enlargement plus a translation.
